messages:
alice.dev: quick q — can we downsample auth/edge logs after 90 days to save on SIEM costs, while keeping enough for vuln triage and forensics?

carlos-sec: short answer: maybe, but need guarantees for incident reconstruction + legal hold. what are we downsampling to? 1%? hourly aggregates? :thinking_face:

julie-sre: on the SRE side we can produce aggregated metrics (counts by user/action) and keep full raw for flagged sessions. sampling 1% becomes useless for forensics. hourly rollups + index-sampling for cold tier looks reasonable.

diana-legal: we need retention baselines per data class. auth failures tied to customer incidents should be preserved un-sampled for at least 1 year if requested via legal/ticket. otherwise we can sample for cost control.

oncall-security: incident workflow note — when an incident is declared, a "sealed snapshot" must be taken immediately (no sampling) and we retain that snapshot until closure + 180d.

alice.dev: ok — proposal: keep 90 days of full fidelity in hot SIEM, 91-365 days in cold tier with 10% raw sampling but with deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by user_id so we can get representative sessions, and >365 days: aggregated rollups only. plus sealed snapshots triggered by incidents or vuln-triage. sound sane?

carlos-sec: deterministic sampling by user_id is better than pure random. still worried about proof for forensics. add a short list of event types that are never sampled: auth success/failure, privilege change, key unwrap, token exchange.

julie-sre: agreed — never-sample list is doable. will also add an alert that auto-triggers a sealed snapshot when those events spike or when a Jira with label `incident:security` is created.

alice.dev: example SIEM export rule i'd use for sealed snapshot (Splunk-ish):
```
index=auth_logs (event_type IN ("login_failure","privilege_change","kms_unwrap")) earliest=-15m latest=now | sort 0 _time | limit 10000
```
use that to create a bounded export that's KMS-wrapped and stored in vault-bucket; access logging retained.

carlos-sec: we should KMS-wrap sealed snapshots with a CMK per-tenant/team and log CMK usage. add ticket to rotate keys every 6 months.

diana-legal: add a checkbox in the sealed snapshot request template: "legal hold required?" — if yes, snapshot retention is extended and access audit must be provided to requestor.

oncall-security: infra-bot FYI will enforce exports >100MB require approval.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: export-policy v1.3 applied to bucket `sealed-snapshots-prod`. Approval required: security-oncall + infra-ops.

julie-sre: action items — I'll draft a sampling config PR (opt-in per-index) and implement deterministic reservoir sampling + never-sample list. blocking question: do we need per-customer sampling profiles?

carlos-sec: yes for enterprise customers with contracts. put per-tenant overrides behind config and default to global policy.

alice.dev: I'll open a ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/SEC-3245 "Sampling+SealedSnapshot policy for logs" with summary and owners: julie-sre (implementation), carlos-sec (policy), diana-legal (compliance). target: RFC by next Tue.

diana-legal: fine, also cc compliance-team on RFC.

alice.dev: thanks all :thumbsup:
